name: manual_bb8f39
claim: Before any destructive git ancestry operation (force-reset, history rewrite, branch deletion), create a safety ref pointing at the commit about to be discarded first, unconditionally — this is what turns a scary 'we might have lost work' moment into a routine cherry-pick-and-reset, and costs nothing to do even when it turns out to be unnecessary.

decisions.notes: When a doctrine-authoring commit was mistakenly pushed to main, the safety ref created before touching anything (safety/main-doctrine-commit-20260713) meant the remediation was a 2-minute cherry-pick-and-reset instead of a recovery investigation. Repeated again during the PR#242 replay: cherry-picking only the real content commit onto fresh main, skipping a no-op backmerge commit, worked cleanly because nothing destructive happened until the safety net was already in place.
